title: Unrealistic emissions scenarios help AI climate models prepare for unfamiliar futures
summary: MIT researchers with Imperial College London designed a small synthetic set of deliberately unrealistic emissions scenarios to train climate emulators, which normally need six to eight full Earth system model runs that each take months. The method needs only one model run, and the emulator predicted unseen scenarios and local pollutant-control effects where traditional emulators failed. It was validated with a simple climate model rather than a full Earth system model, and the article reports no quantitative accuracy metrics.
ai_technology: Climate emulator trained on optimized synthetic scenarios

evidence.tested: An emulator trained on a small set of synthetic scenarios predicted unseen scenarios and a local pollutant-control effect where traditional emulators failed. The source says it was validated with a simple climate model.
evidence.unknown: The source says the method still needs testing on a full Earth system model scenario and on other climate model types; it does not say whether this has been done.
evidence.ai_role: An optimization algorithm generated the synthetic training scenarios; an AI emulator was trained on them to predict climate outcomes.
